opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards vary according to project but will only exceptionally exceed £6,000 and will generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000. Travel grants up to £2,000 per person (13 days or less) or £2,500 per person (14 days or more); up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more. Japan office considers awards up to ¥300,000 for PhD students from Japan travelling to the UK.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects (though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support). Payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts. No support for undergraduate or master's students, or student fees.
opportunities.summary: Seed funding enabling UK-Japan projects that might otherwise not be possible. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges between the two countries, collaborative projects, teaching and development of Japanese language and cultural studies, and academic research, visits and exchange. Projects should bring people in the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding and develop lasting collaboration.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (annual, decision in March of following year)

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 per year; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally be able to show an existing research record; consideration also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields. Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan, be supported by reputable referees not based at the same institution as either project partner, and show evidence of facilities provided by host institutions. Preference to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants.
opportunities.summary: Awards supporting exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK. Broad in application, supporting study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare, and creating opportunities for researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers in both countries to share knowledge and develop new approaches. Grants may be used for travel expenses, conference and publication costs.
